review_notes: Source-first scope: the abstract proposes a new method for estimating the relation between investment and uncertainty of future benefits; the introduction identifies the R&D-versus-capital-expenditure comparison as the central question. Section 4.1 explicitly says Tables 3 and 4 report the main results: Table 3 estimates the relation using current outlays and Table 4 uses capitalized R&D and net PP&E. Table 3 Panels A and B are retained as parallel deflator specifications (BVE and price), and Table 4 Panel B is retained as the co-primary cumulative-investment specification. The full table equations include advertising expense; the reduced Eq. (5) is augmented in most empirical analyses. Other sensitivity specifications and research-design extensions beyond Tables 3 and 4 are excluded.

The paper names annual cross-sectional regressions but not the underlying estimator. The note that the procedure is similar to Fama–MacBeth does not establish that the annual fits use that estimator. Newey–West inference with five lags applies to mean coefficients across the 21 annual fits.
The paper gives aggregate panel counts (Table 3: 42,776 and 40,569; Table 4: 29,408), not exact per-year regression Ns, so sample_size is null for each repeated specification.

The paper gives conflicting leverage descriptions (Eq. (5) p. 7, data definition p. 10, and table notes pp. 15–16). The equations use an explicit natural-log market-value variable, but the Table 3 label says billions while the data formula does not give a conversion factor. The per-share conversion denominator/date is not specified for investment outlays and asset variables.
Winsorization wording differs between the general data section (p. 11) and the table-specific notes (pp. 15–16). The result records the table-specific rule and flags the discrepancy for review.

The capitalized R&D variable uses five years of historical R&D with 20% annual straight-line depreciation, but the paper does not print exact year-by-year weights or the per-share denominator; the variable definition preserves the stated construction and flags these omitted details.
